bull.b: Strong revenue growth combined with higher traffic indicates broad customer demand rather than growth driven only by new locations. Sustained comparable-sales momentum can improve operating leverage, strengthen brand relevance, and support continued expansion over the next several quarters.

A debt-free position with substantial liquidity and positive operating cash flow gives CAVA flexibility to fund restaurant growth, absorb cost volatility, and pursue shareholder returns. Strong cash generation also reduces dependence on external financing as the company scales its footprint.

New-unit productivity above 100% and strong average unit volumes suggest the concept can replicate successfully as the restaurant base expands. This supports management’s plan for 75–77 net new restaurants in 2026 and creates a durable avenue for multi-year revenue growth.

bear.b: Rising food, packaging, and labor costs are directly reducing restaurant-level profitability, while delivery mix adds further expense pressure. If these costs persist, margin recovery may lag sales growth and reduce the earnings contribution from each incremental restaurant.

bear.t: Heavy Reinvestment and Low Free Cash Flow Conversion
bear.b: Positive operating cash flow is not translating fully into free cash flow because CAVA continues to invest heavily in expansion and operations. This limits near-term internally generated funds available for debt reduction, buybacks, or other uses despite improving reported earnings.

The increase in total debt reduces financial flexibility if restaurant growth or comparable sales weaken, even though leverage remains moderate. At the same time, lower returns on equity suggest that recent profitability is generating less value from the capital invested in the business.
